current_example.problem: If $\cot x = 2,$ then what is the value of $\cot (-x+7\pi)?$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\cot{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14264109/assets/6eb672fe024f024f20c7c3c80947d1b47bade8f998e705d6f411ae3f298ecde2.png)

From the graph, we note the following:

- The period of $\cot{x}$ is $\pi.$

- Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\cot{x}$ is an *odd* function, and we have

$$
\cot(-x) = -\cot{x}.
$$

Let's now evaluate our expression:

- Firstly, using the periodicity of $\cot{x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x+7\pi ) & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x+\pi \cdot 7) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x).\end{aligned}
$$

- Secondly, using the oddness of $\cot{x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x) & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡x \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\cot (-x+7\pi)=-2.$
